1:
On my first day back in Beijing, I opened the piece from my first day in Berlin. After writing another track, time seemed to answer itself like this. Winter–spring. A long wait for myself.
This is also the first ritual about unfolding.
2:
The first ritual, an underground world.
A journey of descent.

Slowly, a little emerges.
3: The underground world begins by entering through the basement of a house. Stored in that space are memories we haven't noticed for a long time; they are always in our home, but we are close to forgetting them. This is how we carelessly forget so many things, yet our bodies remember them all, beyond what linear time can count. Will we see a little light?
4: As a child I played a game called MapleStory. Saying so can sound childish, but it is a link in our memory. In it there was a map called “Abandoned City,” whose people matched what a child imagines: adventure. I remembered that I kept dreaming about that game until university, something I've only recalled just now.
5: Memory wanders in circles, always climbing and descending. A spiral staircase. If possible, when it is heard, how many people will step into such a ritual and hear their own memories? Perhaps this is an invitation, a journey.
6: Out of one of them, one was taken away and one was put in. Which one? And which one are we?
7:
Today I want to respond to it.
Is something at the bottom overlapping again — what is a similar experience?
It passes through me and relates to another.
My will lies between them.

(Listening after the mix was done)
I heard a ship sailing on through the sound of a horn; if where we are heading is an iceberg, it seems we would simply drift slowly toward it.
8:
When something that was itself hidden becomes the main one, the narrative it unfolds is completely different.
In this one, I brought the timbre that had been at the bottom of an earlier fragment to the very front; that seemingly marginal image also has something of its own to say.
(After the mix was done)
I heard the desire underneath.
9:
In the course of the dialogue, long waiting and solos appear, and that long space shows itself too.
(After the mix was done)
I realized that because the me of this moment is already different from the me of that time, what I hear is entirely different too — I've almost forgotten that I'm the author, or perhaps I never was.
10:
The first piece in which my voice appears, but not as the main one — as the solo of a looping instrument. I am only one small link in it, playing together with them against that tangled background.

5.12
Before sending it to the group, I'll listen to this music once more. New feelings may surface too. It's like inviting different people to witness a ritual, starting with those who find their own family.
11:
The first and the eleventh interacted, and I could never have imagined these two would interact so harmoniously. I couldn't have conceived it; I discovered it only after putting them together, and it surprised me.

(Here I suddenly wanted to extend an invitation to the group: if you have time, you could choose to listen to one piece a day rather than all at once, letting the echo of one linger for a while before hearing the second. That holds our patience and a space for our own feelings. Perhaps we could release it that way in the end too — lighting one fragment each day, recording the picture that lights up, until the final 108 appear (I need to tell Hui here))
12:
Suddenly a rhythm and a feeling of music appeared that I would never have made before — moving from one stage to the next?
When a timbre I had never seen appears in my life, at first I can't find a suitable place to put it. This is about whether to allow such a temporary “dissonance” to keep growing, and to be heard as part of the response too.
13:
From here on I clearly knew that, while responding to them, I was no longer their author. They began to affect me; they have lives of their own. In this one something is mourning, and some new memories arrive.

(In the days after the mix was done, I realized that the art we are in may be a blessing, a mourning or a love for some absence, or for what is invisible or not allowed — answering the roar at the bottom of memory with sounds and love that come from cracks; those memories that want to be forgotten and also want to be remembered; forgetting and re-remembering speaking to each other 5.12)
14:
How can we allow mutual responses to be intermittent, a process of tuning in and out? Let some of the incoherent also be acknowledged as part of memory.

I realized the bass in this piece is a bit like the bass of “Dinosaur Egg,” which I released before. This too was something I hadn't expected.

In this process I thought each piece's response must use elements of the previous one, and I found that was merely a rule I had set for what counts as a response; in practice they took part in and replied to each other in ways I never expected. (April)
15:
Response — I've begun to dislike this word; I prefer correspondence. Correspondence goes to a larger place, like a space of water underground; without someone carrying a lamp, it can't be heard.
A ritual in which some light goes into a dark space.

(After the mix was done, I happened to be thinking about communication between people, or between people and the world. I realized communication runs through everything — communication of the body, of music — and the interactions between them and the world may also affect us, and we learn from them one by one)
16: I saw the deep blue of the dusk sky, the kind of blue where you can't tell dawn from dusk. I tried to photograph it, but couldn't find that color to share; you have to stand here, your body standing here, and look. On the stairs on my way home, my body began to respond to what I had written earlier — 13 or 14 or 12, I no longer remember the name. I climbed all the way up, my breathing becoming more and more uneven, until in the end I couldn't tell which note it was, but the response happened on the high road up toward home.
17:
What is our distance from war?
Compared with before, the distance has grown closer. How does that awareness affect our lives?
18:
The call within a collective has always existed in memory.
East, lighting a fire, a divine pavilion in the water.
Eagle, flying tiger, python, bear, wild boar, hedgehog, great whale, leopard — auspicious creatures and blessings on the sacred tree, each one abundant, hung everywhere.
19:
A simple reply. Today I watched a film and wanted to send part of what's in it back to yesterday. It's that simple. In this process I keep doubting myself; I know it's influenced by many other voices, saying: can it really be this simple? Why is it getting harder and harder for us to believe in the simplest things? Sometimes it's only breath and heartbeat.

By this point I want to keep adding more and more that's superfluous, as if explaining my own music. I realized this, and let it unfold in its original form.
20:
Can multiple “I”s play together?
From different memories. When put together they differ, and even the dissonant ones answer one another.
21: There are afternoons like that, when everything in the air rises and bubbles upward in stillness; in summer the air above is warm, a longing to rise slowly, rather than a desire to shoot straight up.
23:
The present time and September 2, 2022
Memories are all twisted together. A wet towel.
24:
Today the feeling in my body is mourning.
Things whose reason for being here I don't know are all presented in the music, one by one; I listen quietly.
25: When the first people arrived here, they knew nothing, and didn't know that they didn't know. What they had was endless curiosity, mouths hanging open. Where are we going?
26:
At first we can't see each other; when we recognize each other, “I” and “you” appear as separate, and the first parting is the moment of meeting. That is a piece of expedition.


Today I went to the post-screening talk for the film Binoche made. She said her film is an adventure, inviting the audience, like her, to become creators who understand, feel and think, rather than being told or explained to. I deeply share that feeling. Creating excites me and also stirs my deepest fears, because I often wonder whether such a frequency will be misunderstood. But this has to be gotten through: continuing to share the process with this unease and love, exposing my vulnerability, which also gives others a chance to realize they can allow their own vulnerability. In this, in this, keep going down, always.
27: Tomorrow I'll have a tooth pulled. I've written a sacrificial song for the little tooth and drawn some portraits of it for its funeral. A simple blessing and farewell. Feeling loss. Early people gathered around to bless and perform rituals. Our lives need everyday awareness. reconnect remember
28:
The tooth is out. The frequency that makes a tooth ache.
Some absurd and weak feelings. Some banter.
Serious loss. And the responses to pain from childhood: yelling, or a small retching sound.
All remembered, and all happening at the same time.
Brief, powerful, deep and light memories.


I realized that everything is asking us how to live and where we are going. Putting what we practice together with what we have always not allowed to exist takes courage and adventure.
29: The maxillary sinus is a space, a space sealed by bone. There are melodies inside too, wishes waiting to heal. Waiting with the sincerity and childhood of waiting for Santa Claus to put gifts in a stocking.
30: When I perform, I always turn off the metronome, and I don't intend to align those small rhythmic misalignments. Perhaps you on the other side can hear that someone is playing for you — a person, with their own fear, panic or hesitation.
31:
“Replies That Can't Be Aligned”



Ryuichi Sakamoto kept composing until just before his death. In the last pieces he wrote you can really hear the sighs of a whole life, one after another. A sigh can't be simply defined by any word; a sigh is eternal, and that feeling of life being lived is moving. Connected to that source, day by day bringing out that unsteady feeling at the bottom, perhaps someone will really hear such vastness.
At his last concert, what he played were not perfect notes… they were trembling notes, one by one, yet unerringly accurate to his present moment.

I suddenly realized that if I can say these words from the bottom of my heart, perhaps I'll have a chance to invite more people to join on that website.



This period stopped because of my cat's tumor and my own surgery; life is always in danger.



When I sing and hear the ensemble in the space, my breath becomes very, very long. If I focus only on my own breathing, it becomes short and shallow; even if I wish it were longer, the only thing we can do is to give more space and listen to the ensemble.




66 asked me what I would do if I couldn't communicate in a group. I said it's my intuition: art gives us space, and whenever I have words I can't put into language, I can turn them into a ritual or an action. But it's the same; it still needs that moment of opening one's mouth. I said that moment is an unstructured moment, a subtle sense of danger and a space of experienced failure, and the space of failure is very important. Right now I'm made almost entirely of all kinds of continuous failure. I'm willing to fail completely in every moment, which I was not willing to do before.
32: Spoon is sick. Spoon is a language of love, my only family. Many mixed-up things exist here. When there is no way to use any description, it is no longer a description — it is a becoming.
33: After landing in Haikou, I wrote this in the airport there. I'm waiting for my companions to fly in from another city. The sounds of the terminal hall, and the damp, humid touch this city has already left on my skin. Repeated messages, new messages appear on the loudspeaker. What memories will this draw out in us?
34: This is the first piece I wrote in Hainan: when people gather together, the possibility of flow, the look of fate's horn being blown, the space where each of us plays together with it and converges.
35: A completely new attempt. An inner impulse. What brought me to this moment and this place?
